definition: Optical braille recognition is technology to capture and process images of braille characters into natural language characters.
details: It is used to convert braille documents for people who cannot read them into text, and for preservation and reproduction of the documents.

explainer.lead: Optical braille recognition captures and processes images of braille into natural-language characters. It lets braille documents be read by people who cannot read braille and be preserved and reproduced.

tiers.eli5: A camera takes a picture of braille dots, and software turns them into ordinary text.
tiers.practitioner: It converts scanned or photographed braille into text for accessibility and archival reproduction. Image quality and dot capture are decisive, since the system works from images of the characters.
tiers.paperLevel: It is technology that captures and processes images of braille characters into natural-language characters; its input is images, not tactile cells.

explainer.example: A scanned braille page is photographed, processed, and output as plain text so a sighted reader can understand it.
